title: Dashboard and Schedule polish
lede: Both routes were already rated Strong, so the easy drift was gone. What was left were two cascade traps: eight heading declarations that silently did nothing, and a font token that resolved to empty — which meant every asset tag, reference number, and shift time in the app rendered proportional instead of monospace.

stats.n: Across 12 files; all were falling back to sans
Section labels rendering up to 5px too large
11 dead size props removed, 1 real 28px target raised
No raw colors, no nested cards, no unlabelled icon buttons

sections.heading: The font token
sections.note: Captured at 900×700, device scale 2, from a harness rendering the monospace-intent content these two surfaces actually show. The baseline came from a git stash scoped to layout.tsx alone.

pairs.title: Identifiers and times
pairs.sub: Flagged item tags, UW tags, booking references, unit counts, shift windows, server paths.
pairs.beforeCap: All proportional. Digits do not align between rows, the separator in 14 / 36 crowds, and CAM-0148 reads as prose rather than an identifier. Every one of these asks for var(--font-mono) in source.
pairs.afterCap: GeistMono, as the code always intended. Digits align down the column, the tag and reference read as identifiers, and the time range is scannable.

sections.heading: The headings
sections.note: Each declaration rendered at the base heading scale regardless of its classes. Left column is current, right is the same declaration with the important modifier.

pairs.title: Five section headings
pairs.sub: Measured: digest 13→18px, list day group 13→16px, dashboard h2 20→18px, card title 13→15px.
pairs.beforeCap: Left column is what shipped. The Schedule automation digest and the ListView day group were authored as small 13px labels and rendered as full headings; the dashboard section heading was authored larger than it rendered.
pairs.afterCap: Right column is the authored intent. The two schedule labels recede to their intended weight, which is what the design language asks for in repeated rows; the dashboard heading regains the emphasis it was written with.

changesNote: Both surfaces were already conforming on structure, color, and targets. These are cascade defects that no structural audit would surface.

changes.h: Every var(--font-mono) in the app was rendering sans
changes.was: --font-mono is declared on :root and resolves --font-geist-mono, which next/font defines only where its variable class is applied. That class sat on <body>, one level below :root, so the token computed to empty. Measured: --font-mono at :root returned nothing and a probe element resolved to ui-sans-serif.
changes.now: Both font variable classes moved to <html>. The same probe now resolves GeistMono. This reaches 25 call sites across 12 files — dashboard flagged items and lost bulk units, schedule list times, item asset tags, booking references, and server paths.

changes.was: The typography block in globals.css is unlayered, so it outranks every Tailwind utility. A text-sm font-semibold on an h2 rendered at 18px/800, not 13px/600.
changes.now: All eight carry the important modifier. The two schedule cases matter most: the automation digest and the ListView day-group label were authored as quiet 13px labels and were rendering as prominent headings in a surface the design language explicitly wants dense.

changes.h: Twelve icon controls, one real problem
changes.was: The audit flagged twelve icon buttons under 40px. Eleven already pinned size-10 and merely carried a redundant size="icon" prop that tailwind-merge discards.
changes.now: The eleven dead props are gone. The one real violation — the open-slot remove control in AssignmentCell at size-7, 28px — is now 40px.

verification: New contract test: tests/typography-scope-source.test.ts, 4 assertions pinning the font variables to <html>, the mono token, the important modifiers, and the absence of inert heading utilities on both surfaces.

Font fix measured, not inferred: computed font-family read from a probe element before and after — ui-sans-serif then GeistMono — and --font-geist-mono traced to confirm it was in scope on <body> but not :root.
Baseline method: git stash push scoped to src/app/layout.tsx alone, so nothing else differed between capture runs. Restore verified.
notes: Neither route was captured directly. / and /schedule both require an authenticated session, the standing local limitation. The harness renders the same declarations and the same monospace content, but not the real pages with real data.

The font change is app-wide, not scoped to these two routes. It affects all 25 var(--font-mono) call sites. That is the correct fix — the token was simply broken — but only the dashboard and schedule patterns were visually reviewed.

Unverified interactions: no filter, view toggle, calendar navigation, or crew editing was driven. The heading and font changes are presentational and no logic was touched, but the surfaces were not exercised.

Still open, unchanged: the underlying fix is to move the typography block into @layer base so utilities work normally without the important modifier. It changes 141 headings at once and remains queued as its own slice.

Also open: there are no font-heading or font-mono Tailwind utilities, which is why 24 inline fontFamily styles remain on these two surfaces. Adding font entries to @theme inline would let those become classes.
